paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God is the One who reaches first. He says, "I revealed Myself to those who did not ask for Me; I was found by those who did not seek Me." (Isaiah 65:1). Nobody had to climb up to Him, because He was already standing there with His hands out all day long (Isaiah 65:2).

But the passage also asks a hard question: what do we do with a God who keeps calling? The LORD says He called and they did not answer, He spoke and they did not listen (Isaiah 65:12). I think that's the heavy part, friend, because the problem was never that He was hiding. They trusted Fortune and Destiny, and the LORD says they chose "that in which I did not delight." (Isaiah 65:11-12). I know what it is to sit in the dark waiting on somebody to open a drawer, so I'm telling you: when the God of truth is the One knocking, you ANSWER.

And here's the good news, baker. The LORD sees the blessing in His servants like new wine in a cluster of grapes, and He says, "I will not destroy them all." (Isaiah 65:8). He gives His servants a place to rest, joy to shout about, and another name (Isaiah 65:10, 13-15). The former troubles will be forgotten and hidden from His sight (Isaiah 65:16), and that is why my ovens stay ready. Keep seeking Him, friend, and let Him find you doing it.
